newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen steady as JGBs surge, seen toppish.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen steady as JGBs surge, seen toppish.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures retained a firm tone but failed to extend their gains on Thursday while Japanese government bond (JGB) futures continued to reach for the sky.

"The force that's driving Euroyen and JGBs higher is the cash from Japanese institutions looking for yields and needing to park their funds somewhere. But the yield curve shouldn't be this flat," said a trader with a European bank.
He said JGBs looked very overbought and would be susceptible to a sharp correction if there was any Japanese data, or a comment from an official, indicating a pick-up in the economy.
"The downside is hard to tell because if there's a liquidation kind of move, this thing would have no floor," he added.
December JGBs settled at 125.44 against their previous 125.33 after hitting a new contract high of 125.50.
"JGBs have limited upside scope. They came back off quite quickly after hitting the contract high of 125.50," said a dealer with a European futures house.
The lead June Euroyen contract was at 99.28 in late trade against its IMM close at 99.29. Volume was a low 4,720 lots.
"Euroyen has topped out already, unless you want to price in a rate cut or no rate hike for a year, which would be optimistic," said the bank trader.

Eurodollar futures edged up a notch after a bout of overnight profit-taking, but dealers said the market was unlikely to make any dramatic moves ahead of the U.S. non-farm payrolls report for October, due on Friday.
March Eurodollars finished at 94.43 against their IMM close at 94.42.
